what_happened: Donald Trump reportedly used a catering truck to board a secret military flight from Turkey last month.
The operation was a ruse prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against President Trump.
Trump had initially boarded the older Air Force One jet in front of television cameras at Ankara International Airport.
Minutes later, he was secretly transferred to a smaller US Air Force C-32A aircraft using an airport catering truck.
The older Air Force One served as a decoy, with journalists and some White House staff believing Trump was on board.
The C-32A then flew Trump to Britain.
The arrangement concealed Trump's actual location for several hours, including from some senior administration officials.
The incident occurred after a NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey.
Hostilities between the US and Iran were escalating at the time of the flight.
attribution: The Washington Post reported the operation, citing a US official and corroborating material.
The New York Times corroborated the report.
CBS News also reported on the secret plane switch.
Reuters reported on the incident, citing the Washington Post.
White House communications director Steven Cheung did not directly respond to questions about the decision to switch planes.
verified: Donald Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey.
A catering truck was used to transfer Trump between aircraft.
The secret flight was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat.
The older Air Force One was used as a decoy.
Trump flew to Britain on a C-32A aircraft.
contested: Some White House staff members and journalists on the decoy plane were reportedly unaware of the secret switch.
factbase.notification_line: Donald Trump reportedly used a catering truck to board a secret military flight from Turkey due to an Iranian assassination threat.
